concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
question: Which of the following elements has the largest atomic radius?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rb (Rubidium)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atomic radius:** The atomic radius is the distance from the nucleus to the outermost electrons of an atom. It generally increases down the group in the periodic table due to the addition of electron shells.
 
• **Group 1 elements:** The elements mentioned in the question (Li, Na, K, and Rb) belong to Group 1 of the periodic table, also known as the alkali metals. Their atomic radii increase as we move down the group.
 
• **Explanation of trends:** As we move down the group in the periodic table:
 
 
• The number of electron shells increases, leading to a larger atomic radius.
 
• The effective nuclear charge experienced by the outermost electrons decreases slightly due to increased electron shielding, allowing the outer electrons to be further away from the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of elements:** Among the given elements:
 
 
• **Li (Lithium):** Atomic radius is small as it is the first element in Group 1.
 
• **Na (Sodium):** Atomic radius is larger than Li due to the addition of one more electron shell.
 
• **K (Potassium):** Atomic radius further increases due to an additional electron shell compared to Na.
 
• **Rb (Rubidium):** Atomic radius is the largest among the given elements because it has the most electron shells.
 
 
 
• Hence, **Rubidium (Rb)** has the largest atomic radius among the given elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alkali Metals (Group 1):**

 
 
• Alkali metals include **Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), Potassium (K), Rubidium (Rb), Cesium (Cs), and Francium (Fr).**
 
• They are highly reactive metals and are rarely found in their free form in nature.
 
• They exhibit common properties such as softness, low density, and high reactivity with water.
 
 
 
• **Rubidium (Rb):**
 
 
• **Atomic number:** 37.
 
• **Electron configuration:** [Kr] 5s¹.
 
• **Uses:** Used in atomic clocks, electronics, and research applications.
 
• **Location:** Found in minerals such as lepidolite and pollucite.
 
 
 
• **Trends in Atomic Radius:**
 
 
• Atomic radius increases down a group due to the addition of electron shells.
 
• Atomic radius decreases across a period (left to right) due to increasing nuclear charge attracting electrons closer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Periodic trends:**

 
 
• Atomic radius is influenced by factors such as number of electron shells, nuclear charge, and electron shielding.
 
• In alkali metals, the atomic radius increases significantly down the group due to added electron shells.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Rubidium:**
 
 
• Rubidium salts are used in biochemistry and medical research.
 
• Rubidium vapor is utilized in atomic physics experiments to study Bose-Einstein condensation.
